beats.text: You'd rather get an electric shock than sit alone with your thoughts.
Researchers left students alone in an empty room. No phone. Just their thoughts. For fifteen minutes.
Most of them didn't enjoy it.
Then they added a button that gave a mild electric shock. A shock they had said they'd pay to avoid.
Two out of three men pressed it. And one in four women.
One man pressed it a hundred and ninety times.
So if you grab your phone the second you're alone, you're not weird. Thinking is hard work.

sources: Wilson, Reinhard, Westgate, Gilbert, Ellerbeck, Hahn, Brown & Shaked (2014). Just think: The challenges of the disengaged mind. Science 345(6192). 6-15 min alone; many rated it unpleasant; 67% of men (12/18) and 25% of women (6/24) gave themselves at least one shock they'd earlier said they'd pay to avoid; one outlier shocked himself 190 times (excluded). Via BPS Research Digest.
